t1.text: Mod manager: the built-in UI on the native management interfaces

n1.text:
Launch rule

• A main mod is set → the app opens it. The manager stays one menu item away: watane › Mods… (⇧⌘M).
• None is set → the app opens the manager.
• A mod with main = true in mod.toml becomes main when installed, if none is set. "Make main" in the details chooses any mod with a page.

The manager is one view on native functions; from step 10 a shell mod reaches them through watane:host/manage. Approvals stay in the consent view. (W35, W36)

n2.text:
Design rules

• Two levels: a list (Library, Find, Updates), then one mod.
• One primary action per view; destructive actions are quiet, never the default, and name their consequence.
• Library order: the main mod, then mods that need you, then A–Z.
• Quiet chrome, so the consent view stands out.
• Grant switches act at once here; a managing mod's requests for more open the consent view.
• Tweaks on each artboard: dark; on First start, dropping shows the drop state.
